questions.question: Name three methods of contraception that work in different ways and explain the step of reproduction each one blocks.
questions.expected_answer: Any three, for example: the pill, injection or implant (hormonal) prevents ovulation and thickens cervical mucus; the male or female condom (barrier) prevents sperm reaching the egg; the copper loop (IUD) is toxic to sperm and prevents implantation; vasectomy blocks the sperm ducts; tubal ligation blocks the oviducts; abstinence prevents sperm and egg meeting at all.

questions.question: Explain the difference between HIV and AIDS and list three ways HIV is transmitted and three ways it is not.
questions.expected_answer: HIV is the human immunodeficiency virus, which destroys helper (CD4) white blood cells. AIDS is the late stage of untreated HIV infection, when the immune system is so weak that opportunistic infections such as TB take hold. Transmitted by: unprotected sexual intercourse, sharing needles or razor blades with infected blood, from mother to baby in pregnancy, birth or breastfeeding. Not transmitted by: hugging, shaking hands, sharing cups or toilets, sweat, tears, saliva, mosquito bites.

questions.question: Why do health workers recommend dual protection, and how are bacterial and viral STDs treated differently?
questions.expected_answer: Hormonal methods and the loop prevent pregnancy reliably but give no protection against STDs and HIV, while condoms protect against infections but are less reliable against pregnancy as typically used; using a condom every time together with a reliable method gives protection against both. Bacterial STDs such as syphilis, gonorrhoea and chlamydia are cured with antibiotics and the partner must be treated too; viral STDs such as HIV and herpes cannot be cured but are controlled with medication.
